mainTopic: Valid sandals for חליצה, חליצה at night or on the left foot, and the essential acts of חליצה
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ברייתא listing sandals that cannot be used for חליצה, including a burial sandal made to honor a זקן. רבינא asks why that sandal fails when the בית דין's own sandal is also not walked in. רב אשי answers that a court messenger may walk in the court's sandal, so it counts as a shoe. A new משנה follows: חליצה at night is valid and on the left foot is invalid, and רבי אלעזר holds the opposite on both. The גמרא explains the night dispute as a question of whether חליצה is like the start of a court case or like its verdict. It then tells of רבה בר חייא, who did a חליצה with a slipper, as a single judge, and at night, and of שמואל's criticism. Two explanations are given for what bothered שמואל. For the left foot, עולא learns the right foot from the מצורע, and the גמרא gives two ways to explain why רבי אלעזר does not use that comparison. Finally, a new משנה asks what happens if the woman leaves out reciting, removing the shoe, or spitting.

steps.title: Sandals of a condemned city and of an elder's burial are invalid
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends its list: a sandal from an עיר הנדחת, or a sandal made only to honor a זקן, may not be used for חליצה. If it was used anyway, the חליצה is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: A sandal belonging to a condemned idolatrous city, or a sandal made in honor of an elder, should not be used for חליצה. If she did use it, her חליצה is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: We are at the end of a ברייתא that lists sandals a woman may not use for חליצה. It adds two more cases, and in both of them the חליצה does not count even after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some earlier items in the list only say 'don't do it at the start' but still accept it after the fact. Here the ruling is stronger: the חליצה is פסולה even after it happened. The זקן's sandal was made to honor him at his burial and not for walking, and that detail is what the next step will question.

keyTerms.meaning: A city whose people mostly worshipped idols. It is destroyed together with its property.
A sandal made to honor an elder, meant to be worn when he is buried
The ceremony where the יבמה removes the יבם's shoe, freeing her from יבום

phrases.english: And [a sandal] of a condemned idolatrous city,
and [the sandal] of an elder, made for his honor,
phrases.notes: This sandal was made for him to wear when he is buried, not for walking around.

phrases.english: she should not perform halitza [with it],
and if she did perform halitza,
her halitza is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁל עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת, וְשֶׁל זָקֵן הֶעָשׂוּי לִכְבוֹדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list in the ברייתא of sandals that cannot be used for חליצה. The list began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sandal from an עיר הנדחת, or a burial sandal made to honor a זקן, makes the חליצה invalid even after the fact.

steps.title: רבינא asks: the court's sandal is not for walking either
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי why the זקן's sandal is invalid for not being made for walking. The בית דין's own חליצה sandal is also not made for walking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Why is the elder's honor sandal different, that it is invalid because it is not made for walking? The court's sandal is also not made for walking!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges the reason the ברייתא's ruling is based on. If 'not made for walking' makes a sandal invalid, the court's own sandal should be invalid too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בית דין kept a special sandal just for חליצה ceremonies, and it was not used for everyday walking. So the reason 'not made for walking' seems to disqualify a sandal everyone already accepts as kosher. Either the reason is wrong, or there must be a real difference between the two sandals.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Asks why two cases that seem the same are treated differently

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
What is different about [the sandal of] an elder made for his honor,
that [it is invalid because] it is not made for walking?
The court's [sandal] also
is not made for walking!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: מַאי שְׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason behind the ruling in step 1 about the זקן's sandal.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that the זקן's sandal is invalid because it is not made for walking
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The בית דין's sandal is also not used for walking, yet it is kosher. So 'not made for walking' cannot be the reason to disqualify a sandal.

steps.title: רב אשי: a court messenger may walk in the court's sandal
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that a court messenger who walked in the בית דין's sandal would not be scolded by the judge. So that sandal is still fit for walking.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If a court messenger walked in it, would the judge be upset with him?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge. Nobody would mind if the court's sandal were used for walking, so it really is a walking shoe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is not how the sandal is usually used, but whether it is allowed to be used for walking. A court messenger may walk in the court's sandal without objection. The זקן's burial sandal is set aside for the dead and is not meant for walking at all, so it does not count as a real shoe for חליצה.
steps.whatToRemember: A sandal counts for חליצה if it is allowed to be walked in, even if it is usually kept for the ceremony. A burial sandal made only to honor a זקן is not meant for walking, so it is פסול.

phrases.english: He said to him:
If [someone] walked in it,
a messenger of the court,
would the judge be upset with him?
phrases.notes: Asked as a question that answers itself: of course the judge wouldn't mind.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִילּוּ מְסַגֵּי בֵּיהּ שְׁלוּחָא דְּבֵי דִּינָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a real difference between the two cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sandals are not used for walking, so they should get the same ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: The court's sandal may be walked in without anyone objecting, so it is a real shoe. The burial sandal is not meant for walking at all, so it is invalid.

steps.title: New משנה: חליצה at night and on the left foot
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: חליצה done at night is valid, but רבי אלעזר says it is invalid. חליצה done on the left foot is invalid, but רבי אלעזר says it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If she performed חליצה at night, her חליצה is valid, and רבי אלעזר invalidates it. If she did it on the left foot, her חליצה is invalid, and רבי אלעזר validates it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with two disagreements about how חליצה must be done. In each case, רבי אלעזר disagrees with the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first case asks whether חליצה, done in front of a בית דין, must happen during the day the way court cases do. The second case asks whether the left foot can be used instead of the right. The first opinion accepts night but rejects the left foot, and רבי אלעזר holds the opposite on both.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up who holds what. The first opinion says night is OK and the left foot is not. רבי אלעזר says the opposite in both cases.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
If she performed halitza at night,
her halitza is valid,
and Rabbi Elazar invalidates it.
[If she did it] on the left [foot],
her halitza is invalid,
and Rabbi Elazar validates it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: the time and the foot used for חליצה, after the discussion of valid sandals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First opinion: חליצה at night is valid, and on the left foot it is invalid. רבי אלעזר: at night it is invalid, and on the left foot it is valid.

steps.title: Suggesting that the dispute depends on comparing court cases to נגעים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי אלעזר compares court cases to נגעים, which are judged only by day, and the תנא קמא does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Shall we say this is their argument? One master holds that we compare court disputes to נגעים, and the other master holds that we do not compare court disputes to נגעים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a reason for the argument in the משנה about doing חליצה at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נגעים may only be judged in the daytime. If court cases, including חליצה, follow the same rule, then חליצה at night would be invalid, which is רבי אלעזר's view. The תנא קמא would hold there is no such comparison, so night is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion that may be rejected)
we compare (two areas of law so that the same rules apply)
leprous afflictions, judged by a כהן

phrases.english: Gemara:
Shall we say that they disagree about this:
that one master holds we compare court disputes to leprous afflictions,
phrases.notes: נגעים can only be checked in the daytime (ויקרא 13:14), so comparing the two would make court cases daytime-only too.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר לָא מַקְּשִׁינַן רִיבִים לִנְגָעִים?
phrases.english: and the other master holds we do not compare court disputes to leprous afflictions?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes the reasoning behind the night-time dispute in the משנה of step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What underlying principle divides רבי אלעזר and the תנא קמא on חליצה at night?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suggestion: רבי אלעזר compares ריבים to נגעים (daytime only); the תנא קמא does not.

steps.title: Rejecting the comparison: is חליצה like the start of a case or its verdict?
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees there is no full comparison to נגעים. The real argument is whether חליצה is like the start of a case or like the verdict.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone holds that we do not compare court disputes to נגעים. If we did, even a verdict could not be given at night. Here they disagree about this: one master holds חליצה is like the start of a case, and the other master holds חליצה is like the verdict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 5 and gives a new explanation of the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If court cases were fully compared to נגעים, even the verdict would have to be given by day. But we know a verdict may be given at night. So both sides agree that only the start of a case must be by day. רבי אלעזר treats חליצה like the start of a case, so it is invalid at night. The תנא קמא treats it like the verdict, so it is valid at night.

keyTerms.meaning: the verdict, the end of a court case
the start of a court case
is similar to, is treated like

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that the start of a case must be in the daytime and the verdict may be at night. They only disagree about which of the two חליצה resembles.
steps.whatToRemember: The dispute is not about comparing to נגעים. It is about whether חליצה is like תחלת דין (daytime only) or גמר דין (night is fine).

phrases.english: No:

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא מַקְּשִׁינַן רִיבִים לִנְגָעִים,
phrases.english: everyone holds that we do not compare court disputes to leprous afflictions,
for if we compared them,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ גְּמַר דִּין בַּלַּיְלָה נָמֵי לָא,
phrases.english: even a verdict at night would also not be allowed,
phrases.notes: The point is that in money cases a verdict may be given at night, so there clearly is no full comparison.

phrases.english: and here, they disagree about this:

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: חֲלִיצָה כִּתְחִלַּת דִּין דָּמְיָא,
phrases.english: one master holds: חליצה is like the start of a court case,
phrases.notes: This is רבי אלעזר, who says חליצה at night is invalid.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: חֲלִיצָה כִּגְמַר דִּין דָּמְיָא.
phrases.english: and the other master holds: חליצה is like the verdict of a court case.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא מַקְּשִׁינַן רִיבִים לִנְגָעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 5's proposal and replaces it with a new reason for the dispute.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the dispute depends on comparing ריבים to נגעים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A full comparison would forbid even a verdict at night, which is permitted, so no one holds a full comparison.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute is whether חליצה resembles תחלת דין or גמר דין.

steps.title: רבה בר חייא's חליצה with a slipper, one judge, at night, and שמואל's criticism
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר חייא קטוספאה did a חליצה with a soft slipper, with only one judge, and at night. שמואל mocked him for following lone opinions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר חייא of Ctesiphon performed a חליצה with a slipper, alone, and at night. שמואל said: How great is the strength of this man, who acts like a lone opinion!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story of a חליצה done in three unusual ways and records שמואל's sharp criticism.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the three details is a point where some opinion would invalidate the חליצה. שמואל claims that by doing this, רבה בר חייא relied on minority opinions that are not the accepted הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: a soft slipper, not made of leather
alone, with only one judge instead of a court
a lone opinion, a minority view

phrases.english: Rabba bar Ḥiyya of Ctesiphon
performed a חליצה with a slipper,
and alone, and at night.
phrases.notes: "Alone" means he was the only judge, without a full בית דין.

phrases.english: שמואל said:
How great is this man's strength, that he acts like a lone opinion!
phrases.notes: שמואל is being sarcastic. He is criticizing, not praising.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר חִיָּיא קְטוֹסְפָאָה עֲבַד עוֹבָדָא בְּמוּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the theory of the night-time dispute to a practical case involving night and other unusual details.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל disapproves of a חליצה done with a מוק, by a single judge, and at night, calling it following lone opinions.

steps.title: Asking what bothered שמואל, since the slipper and the night ruling are unnamed teachings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what שמואל objected to. A slipper and night-time חליצה are both allowed by unnamed teachings, which usually means they are the accepted halacha.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is difficult? If it is the slipper, an unnamed teaching allows it. If it is the night, an unnamed teaching allows it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's criticism and sets up an explanation of what he meant, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unnamed (סתם) teaching usually means it is the majority view, not a lone opinion. Using a מוק is approved by an unnamed teaching, and our משנה from step 4 allows night-time חליצה without naming anyone. So why did שמואל say רבה בר חייא followed lone opinions?

keyTerms.meaning: it is taught as an unnamed teaching (usually the accepted view)

phrases.english: What is difficult?
phrases.notes: In other words: what exactly was שמואל upset about?

phrases.english: If it is the slipper, an unnamed teaching allows it.
If it is the night, an unnamed teaching allows it.
phrases.notes: This is our משנה from step 4, which allows חליצה at night without naming anyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קַשְׁיָא? אִי מוּק סְתָמָא תַּנְיָא
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that רבה בר חייא followed lone opinions
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both the slipper and night-time חליצה are allowed by unnamed teachings, which reflect the majority view, so they are not lone opinions.

steps.title: The real problem was the single judge
steps.stepSummary: שמואל was not bothered by the slipper or the night. He was bothered that רבה בר חייא used only one judge, which follows a lone opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was the single judge that bothered him: how could he do it with just one judge, when only a lone opinion allows that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 8. Out of the three details, only the one-judge part was a problem for שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slipper and the night are both allowed by unnamed teachings, so they are fine. Doing חליצה with a single judge is different, because only a lone תנא allows it. Following a lone תנא against the majority is what שמואל mocked.

keyTerms.meaning: a lone opinion, one Tanna against the majority
it was difficult for him, it bothered him

phrases.english: Rather, it was the "single judge" that bothered him:
phrases.notes: "Him" means שמואל, who mocked רבה בר חייא in Step 7.

phrases.english: how could he do it with a single judge,
when that is taught only by a lone opinion?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8 by narrowing שמואל's complaint to one detail.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing: only one of the three details was the target of the criticism.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל seemed to object to all three details, even though two of them are allowed by unnamed teachings.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל objected only to the one-judge חליצה, since that follows a lone opinion.

steps.title: Proof that a one-judge חליצה is a lone opinion
steps.stepSummary: A משנה shows that only רבי עקיבא allowed a חליצה with no proper court, and רב נחמן rules that the halacha does not follow the lenient view.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: if she did חליצה before two or three judges, and one turned out to be a relative or disqualified, the חליצה is invalid. רבי שמעון and רבי יוחנן הסנדלר say it is valid. There was a case of a man who did חליצה with her alone, in prison, and רבי עקיבא declared it valid. רב יוסף בר מניומי said in the name of רב נחמן: the הלכה does not follow that pair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove that doing חליצה with a single judge is a lone opinion. It adds רב נחמן's ruling that we do not follow the lenient view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The unnamed first opinion requires a proper court, so if one judge is disqualified the חליצה is invalid. רבי שמעון and רבי יוחנן הסנדלר are lenient, and רבי עקיבא went even further and approved a חליצה with no judges at all. רב נחמן rules against the lenient pair, so relying on a single judge goes against the accepted הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: a relative, who may not serve as a judge

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why שמואל was so sharp. רבה בר חייא relied on an opinion that the halacha explicitly rejects.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:
If she did חליצה before two or three judges

phrases.aramaic: וְנִמְצָא אֶחָד מֵהֶן קָרוֹב אוֹ פָּסוּל
phrases.english: and one of them turned out to be a relative or disqualified,
her חליצה is invalid.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הַסַּנְדְּלָר מַכְשִׁירִים.
phrases.english: And רבי שמעון and רבי יוחנן הסנדלר declare it valid.
And there was a case of one man who did חליצה
between him and her alone, in prison,

phrases.aramaic: וּבָא מַעֲשֶׂה לִפְנֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְהִכְשִׁיר.
phrases.english: and the case came before רבי עקיבא, and he declared it valid.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי [אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן]:
phrases.english: And רב יוסף בר מניומי said [in the name of רב נחמן]:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in square brackets, which makes it רב נחמן's ruling, passed on by רב יוסף בר מניומי.

phrases.english: The halacha does not follow that pair.
phrases.notes: "That pair" is רבי שמעון and רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, the lenient opinion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim of Step 9 that a one-judge חליצה is only a lone opinion.
steps.raayaObject: That doing חליצה with a single judge is a lone, rejected opinion.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a disqualified judge, the story of רבי עקיבא in prison, and רב נחמן's ruling against the lenient pair.

steps.title: Another answer: all three details are a lone opinion
steps.stepSummary: A second answer says that the slipper, the single judge and the night are all taught together by one lone תנא, so שמואל objected to all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: all of them too are taught by a lone opinion. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי said, I saw רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע do a חליצה with a soft slipper, alone, and at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to answer Step 8. Here שמואל's complaint covers all three details, not just the single judge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא reports one Sage who did all three things together. That suggests the whole combination is his own personal view, against the other Sages. So רבה בר חייא followed one lone Sage on every point, and that is what שמואל mocked.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you want, say (an alternative answer)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to why שמואל objected. (1) Only the single judge was a problem, since only a lone opinion allows it and the halacha rejects it. (2) All three details come from one lone Sage, רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע.
steps.confusionAlert: The second answer does more than criticize the combination. Since one Sage is reported doing all three together, it treats each of these details, including the slipper and the night, as that individual's view, against the other Sages.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
all of them too are taught by a lone opinion.
phrases.notes: "All of them" means all three details: the slipper, the single judge and the night.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנִי רָאִיתִי אֶת רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן אֱלִישָׁע
phrases.english: I saw רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע
do a חליצה with a soft slipper, alone, and at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, broader answer to the question of Step 8, instead of the narrow answer of Steps 9-10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative answer: the whole combination is shown to be one individual's opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The slipper and night details seemed to follow accepted unnamed teachings.
steps.terutzMaskana: All three details together come from the lone practice of רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע, so שמואל objected to all of them.

steps.title: Why do the Rabbis require the right foot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's ruling that חליצה on the left foot is invalid and asks for the Rabbis' source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if חליצה was done on the left foot, her חליצה is invalid. What is the Rabbis' reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה from Step 4, the left foot. It asks why the Rabbis say a left-foot חליצה does not count, and the next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about חליצה only says "his foot" and does not say which foot. So the Rabbis must have some source for requiring the right foot. רבי אלעזר, who allows the left foot, apparently does not accept that source.

phrases.english: "On the left, her חליצה..." and so on.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from Step 4: חליצה on the left foot is invalid, but רבי אלעזר says it is valid.

phrases.english: What is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבה בר חייא discussion and opens the topic of the left foot from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the Rabbis' rule that חליצה must be done on the right foot.

steps.title: עולא: learn 'foot' from the מצורע
steps.stepSummary: עולא says the word 'foot' in חליצה is compared to the word 'foot' by the מצורע, where the right foot is stated, so חליצה also needs the right foot.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: we learn the word 'foot' here from the word 'foot' by the מצורע. Just as there it is the right foot, so too here it is the right foot.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question. The Rabbis learn the right foot from the laws of the מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a word-comparison, where the same word in two places teaches that the two laws share a detail. By the purification of a מצורע the Torah says to put blood on the big toe of the right foot. Since חליצה also uses the word 'foot', it too must be done on the right foot.

phrases.english: עולא said:
We learn "foot" here from "foot" by the מצורע.
Just as there it is the right foot,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:14

phrases.english: so too here it is the right foot.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא יָלְפִינַן רֶגֶל רֶגֶל מִמְּצוֹרָע
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A word-comparison of 'foot' with the מצורע, where the right foot is stated.

steps.title: But רבי אלעזר also learns from the מצורע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if רבי אלעזר allows the left foot, it seems he does not learn from the מצורע. But a ברייתא shows he does learn the right ear for a slave's piercing from the מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי אלעזר not learn 'foot' from the מצורע? But a ברייתא teaches that רבי אלעזר says: How do we know that the piercing of a slave's ear is on the right ear? 'Ear' is said here, and 'ear' is said there. Just as there it is the right, so too here it is the right!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אלעזר's position. He uses the very same kind of comparison to the מצורע in another case, so why not here?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי אלעזר allows the left foot, it seems he rejects the comparison to the מצורע. Yet for piercing a slave's ear he compares 'ear' to the מצורע's right ear. If he accepts the method there, he should accept it for 'foot' in חליצה too. Steps 15 and 16 give two different answers.

keyTerms.meaning: but wasn't it taught in a ברייתא? (opens a challenge)
piercing the ear of a Hebrew slave who chooses to stay

phrases.english: And does רבי אלעזר not learn
"foot" from "foot" by the מצורע?
But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא:
רבי אלעזר says:
From where do we know that the piercing
phrases.notes: This is piercing the ear of a Hebrew slave who wants to stay with his master (שמות 21:6).

phrases.english: is done on the right ear?
"Ear" is said here,
and "ear" is said there.
phrases.notes: "There" means by the מצורע, where the Torah says the right ear.

phrases.english: Just as there it is the right,
so too here it is the right!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לָא יָלֵיף רֶגֶל רֶגֶל מִמְּצוֹרָע וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's position in light of עולא's source for the Rabbis.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that a left-foot חליצה is valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר uses a word-comparison to the מצורע for the right ear in רציעה, so he should use the same comparison for the right foot in חליצה.

steps.title: The opinions are switched
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers the contradiction by saying the names in the dispute are reversed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the opinions are reversed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer to the contradiction about רבי אלעזר. It says the names were switched, so רבי אלעזר is really the one who requires the right foot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that רבי אלעזר learns the right ear from the מצורע but seems to ignore the מצורע for the foot. If we switch the names, רבי אלעזר requires the right foot too. Now he learns from the מצורע in both cases and stays consistent.

keyTerms.meaning: The opinions are reversed. The names attached to each view are switched.
A leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
The opinions are reversed.
phrases.notes: He means the names in the left-foot dispute are switched, so רבי אלעזר is the one who rules it invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14 by switching the names in the dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Switching the attribution of the opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר allows the left foot yet learns the right ear from the מצורע, which looks inconsistent.
steps.terutzMaskana: The names are switched; רבי אלעזר requires the right foot, so he consistently learns from the מצורע.

steps.title: Ear words are free, foot words are not
steps.stepSummary: רבא keeps the names as they are and explains that the 'ear' comparison is stronger than the 'foot' comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really, do not reverse the opinions. The words 'ear' and 'ear' are extra and free for learning, but the words 'foot' and 'foot' are not free.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer. He leaves the names alone and shows that the two comparisons are not equally strong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה built on words that are extra on both sides cannot be broken by any challenge. The word 'ear' is extra in both places, so רבי אלעזר uses it. The word 'foot' is not extra in both places, so that comparison can still be challenged, and רבי אלעזר does not rely on it.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, do not reverse the opinions
Free, meaning extra words the Torah left open to be used for a גזירה שוה
Learning a law from one place to another because the same word appears in both

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the foot comparison is useless. He is saying it is weaker, because a comparison that is not free on both sides can be knocked down by a good challenge.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Actually, do not reverse the opinions,
"ear" and "ear" are free,
phrases.notes: "Free" means extra: the word "ear" by the slave's piercing and the word "ear" by the מצורע are both extra in their verses.

phrases.english: "foot" and "foot" are not free.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to step 14 that keeps the original names.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Telling apart the strength of two גזירה שוה comparisons
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both comparisons to the מצורע should work the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ear comparison uses free words and cannot be broken; the foot comparison does not, so רבי אלעזר does not rely on it.

steps.title: What challenge breaks the foot comparison?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what challenge could knock down the foot comparison, even if it is not free.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if the words are not free, what challenge is there to break the comparison?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא. A comparison that is not free can only be dropped if there is a real challenge, so which challenge is it? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Words that are not free do not cancel a גזירה שוה on their own. They only mean that a good challenge can break it. So רבא must show an actual challenge against comparing חליצה to the מצורע.

keyTerms.meaning: A challenge that shows the two cases are different, which breaks the comparison

phrases.english: And even if they are not free,
what refutation is there?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי לָא מוּפְנֵי, מַאי פִּירְכָא אִיכָּא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the foot comparison is not used
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not being free is not enough to drop a גזירה שוה; there must be a real challenge, and none has been named.

steps.title: The מצורע is special
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names the challenge: the מצורע needs cedarwood, hyssop and scarlet thread, so he is a special case.
steps.simpleTranslation: It can be challenged: what about a מצורע, who is special because he needs cedarwood, hyssop and scarlet thread?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question by giving the challenge. The מצורע has unusual requirements, so we cannot assume חליצה follows his rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The purification of a מצורע has many special details, like cedarwood, hyssop and scarlet thread. Because his case is so detailed, needing the right foot might be special to him too. That breaks the foot comparison, so according to רבי אלעזר a left-foot חליצה can still be valid.

keyTerms.meaning: What about a מצורע? This opens a challenge showing his case is different.
Cedarwood, hyssop and scarlet thread, used in purifying a מצורע

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, רבי אלעזר learns the right ear from the מצורע because those words are free. He does not learn the right foot, because that comparison is broken by the special rules of the מצורע.

phrases.english: It can be refuted:
what about a leper,
since he requires cedarwood
and hyssop and scarlet thread.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:4

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by naming the challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the source case is special (פירכא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There is no challenge, so the foot comparison should stand.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מצורע's special requirements break the comparison, so according to רבי אלעזר, חליצה does not have to be on the right foot.

steps.title: Which parts of חליצה are essential
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches what happens if the woman leaves out reciting, removing the shoe, or spitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If she removed the shoe and spat but did not recite, her חליצה is valid. If she recited and spat but did not remove the shoe, her חליצה is invalid. If she removed the shoe and recited but did not spit, רבי אליעזר says it is invalid and רבי עקיבא says it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists three cases where one of the three acts of חליצה is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving out the reciting does not ruin the חליצה. Leaving out the removal of the shoe does ruin it, since that is the core act. Leaving out the spitting is a dispute: רבי אליעזר says it is required, and רבי עקיבא says it is not.

keyTerms.meaning: She removed the shoe of the יבם
She recited the verses said at חליצה

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה sets up the next discussion about which acts of חליצה are needed for it to work.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If she removed the shoe and spat,
but did not recite —
her חליצה is valid.
If she recited and spat,
but did not remove the shoe —
her חליצה is invalid.
If she removed the shoe and recited,
but did not spit —
Rabbi Eliezer says: her חליצה is invalid,
Rabbi Akiva says: her חליצה is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ חָלְצָה וְרָקְקָה, אֲבָל לֹא קָרְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion about the right foot ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without reciting, חליצה is valid. Without removing the shoe, it is invalid. Without spitting, רבי אליעזר says invalid and רבי עקיבא says valid.
